600:  * If the bit overflows the user internal representation, no operation
601:  * is performed. As a side effect of calling this function with a value of
602:  * zero, the user flag ALLCOMMANDS is cleared since it is no longer possible
603:  * to skip the command bit explicit test. */

605:     uint64_t word, bit;

615: /* Remove a rule from the retained command rules. Always match rules
616:  * verbatim, but also remove subcommand rules if we are adding or removing the 
617:  * entire command. */
618: void ACLSelectorRemoveCommandRule(aclSelector *selector, sds new_rule) {
619:     size_t new_len = sdslen(new_rule);
620:     char *existing_rule = selector->command_rules;
621: 
622:     /* Loop over the existing rules, trying to find a rule that "matches"
623:      * the new rule. If we find a match, then remove the command from the string by
624:      * copying the later rules over it. */
625:     while(existing_rule[0]) {
626:         /* The first character of the rule is +/-, which we don't need to compare. */
627:         char *copy_position = existing_rule;
628:         existing_rule += 1;
629: 
630:         /* Assume a trailing space after a command is part of the command, like '+get ', so trim it
631:          * as well if the command is removed. */
632:         char *rule_end = strchr(existing_rule, ' ');
633:         if (!rule_end) {
634:             /* This is the last rule, so it it to the end of the string. */
635:             rule_end = existing_rule + strlen(existing_rule);
636: 
637:             /* This approach can leave a trailing space if the last rule is removed,
638:              * but only if it's not the first rule, so handle that case. */
639:             if (copy_position != selector->command_rules) copy_position -= 1;
640:         }
641:         char *copy_end = rule_end;
642:         if (*copy_end == ' ') copy_end++;
643: 
644:         /* Exact match or the rule we are comparing is a subcommand denoted by '|' */
645:         size_t existing_len = rule_end - existing_rule;
646:         if (!memcmp(existing_rule, new_rule, min(existing_len, new_len))) {
647:             if ((existing_len == new_len) || (existing_len > new_len && (existing_rule[new_len]) == '|')) {
648:                 /* Copy the remaining rules starting at the next rule to replace the rule to be
649:                  * deleted, including the terminating NULL character. */
650:                 memmove(copy_position, copy_end, strlen(copy_end) + 1);
651:             }
652:         }
653:         existing_rule = copy_end;
654:     }
655: 
656:     /* There is now extra padding at the end of the rules, so clean that up. */
657:     sdsupdatelen(selector->command_rules);
658: }
